daily.brief: 過去約29小時有62則帖、29個帳號，討論量比昨日稍多。共同看好集中在$INTC同$IREN，各有2個帳號。共同看淡只有$ORCL。最多人講嘅係$NVDA（13次提及、8個帳號），但情緒未夠清晰。最大變化係MSFT減租舊容量嘅敘事繼續發酵，同時INTC喺相同股價水平被重新定價成美國先進晶片製造核心。
daily.full:
共識

共同看好相對清楚。$INTC 有2個帳號：@StockSavvyShay 指出8年前每股55美元時主要係x86 CPU同PC業務，冇外部代工或有意義AI增長引擎；今日同樣55美元，已成為美國推動國內先進晶片製造嘅核心（原帖）。@TrendSpider 提到CEO冇迴避下跌，剛剛又增持約1000萬美元股票，RSI處於2年以上低點，並首次自20美元/股以來出現投降信號（原帖）。$IREN 同樣2個看好：@aleabitoreddit 喺Mirantis收購同最近業績後，從基本面轉正面，經營前景同融資能力更具吸引力，但對現有60億美元ATM（剩23.7億）持謹慎態度（原帖）。@StockSavvyShay 則提到MSFT逐步減少從$ORCL租用較舊$NVDA容量、審視數十億雲端交易，更像轉向更新GPU而非退出AI支出，並要求$IREN升級GB300網絡（原帖）。

共同看淡

$ORCL 係唯一共同看淡，2個帳號。@StockSavvyShay 解釋MSFT減租舊容量同審視交易，@ripster47 直接說微軟正逐步減少甲骨文租用AI雲端容量，並拋售$SOXL（原帖）。@Mr_Derivatives 中性列出包括$ORCL在內多隻股票創52週新低。

分歧

今日無明確分歧（split_total為0）。$NVDA 提及最多（13次、8帳號），但只有1個明確看好帳號，其餘多係技術水平或相關供應鏈討論。@charliebilello 提供修正低點相對歷史高點跌幅數據，包括$NVDA -26%、$TSM -28%等，屬中性觀察（原帖）。

其他值得留意

@SJosephBurns 強調市場關鍵技術水平非常重要，會出每日/每週圖表水平，涵蓋$SPY $QQQ $AMD $NVDA 等。$QQQ 同$SPY 各有5次提及，但情緒偏淡或中性。整體62帖中，共同共識只落在少數個股，大盤討論仍以技術位為主。

weekly.full:
共識

$SPCX 有5個帳號看好。@KobeissiLetter 指Anthropic不再預期2026年市值超過SpaceX成為最大IPO，市場機會從62%跌至28%，伴隨高垃圾信用評級報告。$AAPL 有3個：@MarkNewtonCMT 承認短期動能不穩、過去一個月給短線警告，但較大趨勢穩健無明顯惡化，本週弱勢可能短暫；@munster_gene 強調12月收入指引優於華爾街預期，比略軟利潤率指引重要。$COHR 3個看好：@michaelsikand 指光子學逆向交易，CEO說需求無減弱跡象、2027基本上已預訂滿、客戶訂到2028。$AEHR 同樣3個，因財報強勁（EPS 0.28對0.11、營收3300萬對2700萬、上調展望）。$SKHY 有2個，提到DRAM產能擴張仍不足完整AI情境。

共同看淡

$ASTS 有3個看淡。@KeithMcCullough 做多Allstate、做空$ASTS。$CRWV 有2個看淡，@KeithMcCullough 重申做空。$CBRS 有2個，首次跌破100美元，內部人士可出售股份等壓力。

分歧

$TSLA、$INTC、$ORCL、$QQQ、$MU 等共23隻出現分歧。$ORCL 特別明顯：@WallStJesus 轉Stephens從平等權重升至超配、目標價從185美元上調至213美元（原帖，本週數據），但@StockSavvyShay 同@ripster47 都在講MSFT逐步減少租用舊$NVDA容量。$QQQ 有@OptionsHawk 報告大額看漲期權買入，同時有風險管理喊單。$INTC 延續每日嘅多頭理由（CEO增持、重新定位），但亦有其他看淡聲音。

其他值得留意

$GOOG 有2個看好，提到TPU每美元性能改進同Gemini成本優勢。整體513帖顯示討論集中在AI基建相關個股同大盤技術位，共同看淡只有3隻，分歧遠多於單邊共識。

今日簡報

過去約29小時討論量升至62帖。最清楚嘅共識係$INTC：兩個帳號都從相同55美元水平重新解讀，一個強調已成美國先進晶片製造核心，另一個點出CEO剛增持1000萬美元同RSI極端低位。$IREN 同樣有兩個看好，聚焦收購後基本面改善同MSFT要求升級GB300，但對ATM規模仍有保留。唯一共同看淡係$ORCL，MSFT減租舊$NVDA容量嘅敘事繼續被@StockSavvyShay 同@ripster47 提起。$NVDA 提及最多但情緒未形成單邊。7日視角顯示$SPCX、$AAPL、$COHR 有較乾淨共識，而$ORCL 目標價上調至213美元同減租消息形成對比；28日則$SOFI 最穩，指數同部分AI基建名字仍高度分裂。

daily.brief: Over the past ~29 hours there were 62 posts from 29 accounts, a bit busier than yesterday. Common bullish views sit on $INTC and $IREN, each with 2 accounts. The only common bearish name is $ORCL. $NVDA is the most mentioned (13 times, 8 accounts) but sentiment is not yet clear. The clearest shift remains the MSFT capacity-reduction narrative, while $INTC at the same $55 level is being re-priced as a core for U.S. advanced chip manufacturing.
daily.full:
Consensus

Common bullish views are relatively clear. $INTC has 2 accounts: @StockSavvyShay notes that eight years ago at $55 it was mainly x86 CPU and PC business with no external foundry or meaningful AI growth engine; today at the same $55 it has become central to the U.S. push for domestic advanced chip manufacturing (post). @TrendSpider highlights that the CEO did not avoid the drop and just bought roughly another $10 million of stock, with RSI at a 2-year low and the first capitulation signal since $20 (post). $IREN also has 2: @aleabitoreddit turned fundamentally positive after the Mirantis acquisition and recent results, seeing better operating outlook and financing capacity, though cautious on the remaining $2.37B of the $6B ATM (post). @StockSavvyShay notes MSFT gradually reducing older $NVDA capacity from $ORCL and reviewing tens of billions in cloud deals looks more like a shift to newer GPUs, and that MSFT is asking $IREN to upgrade its GB300 network (post).

Common Bearish

$ORCL is the only common-bearish name, with 2 accounts. @StockSavvyShay explains the MSFT reduction and deal review; @ripster47 directly says Microsoft is gradually reducing AI cloud capacity leased from Oracle and sells $SOXL (post). @Mr_Derivatives neutrally lists several names including $ORCL hitting 52-week lows.

Divergence

No clear splits today (split_total 0). $NVDA is the most mentioned (13 times, 8 accounts) but only one clear bullish account; the rest are technical levels or related supply-chain talk. @charliebilello provides drawdown-from-high data including $NVDA -26%, $TSM -28%, a neutral observation (post).

Other Notes

@SJosephBurns stresses that key technical levels matter a lot and will publish daily/weekly chart levels covering $SPY $QQQ $AMD $NVDA etc. $QQQ and $SPY each have 5 mentions, mostly cautious or neutral. Of the 62 posts, common consensus sits on a few names while index talk remains technical-level focused.

weekly.full:
Consensus

$SPCX has 5 bullish accounts. @KobeissiLetter notes Anthropic no longer expects to surpass SpaceX in market value as the largest 2026 IPO, with the probability dropping from 62% to 28% alongside high junk credit ratings. $AAPL has 3: @MarkNewtonCMT admits short-term momentum is shaky and the past month warned short-term traders, but the larger trend remains solid with no clear deterioration so this week’s weakness may be temporary; @munster_gene stresses that December revenue guidance better than Wall Street expected matters more than the slightly softer margin guide. $COHR has 3: @michaelsikand calls photonics a ready-made reverse trade; the CEO says no signs of demand weakening, 2027 essentially booked out, customers booking into 2028. $AEHR likewise has 3 on a strong print (EPS $0.28 vs $0.11, revenue $33M vs $27M, raised outlook). $SKHY has 2, noting DRAM capacity expansion still falls short of full AI scenarios.

Common Bearish

$ASTS has 3 bearish accounts. @KeithMcCullough is long Allstate and short $ASTS. $CRWV has 2 bearish, with @KeithMcCullough reiterating the short. $CBRS has 2, including the first break below $100 and insider selling windows.

Divergence

$TSLA, $INTC, $ORCL, $QQQ, $MU and others total 23 splits. $ORCL stands out: @WallStJesus relays Stephens raising it from Equal-Weight to Overweight and lifting the target from $185 to $213, while @StockSavvyShay and @ripster47 discuss MSFT gradually reducing older $NVDA capacity. $QQQ has large call buying reported by @OptionsHawk alongside risk-management calls. $INTC continues the daily bullish framing (CEO buying, re-positioning) but also draws other views.

Other Notes

$GOOG has 2 bullish accounts citing TPU cost-per-performance improvements and Gemini cost advantages. Overall 513 posts show discussion concentrated on AI-infrastructure names and index technical levels; only 3 common-bearish names exist while splits far outnumber one-sided consensus.

The list spans financials, healthcare, equipment and more, showing consensus is not confined to semiconductors.

Common Bearish

$RDDT is the most concentrated bearish name. $BA, $FTNT, $RBLX, $HYG and others also draw multiple bearish accounts. These tend to reflect specific fundamentals or industry pressure rather than pure index sentiment.

$SPY is the discussion-volume king with 576 mentions and near-even bull/bear splits. $CRWV is heavily bearish. $TSLA, $SPCX, $MU, $QQQ and others show clear tugs-of-war. $INTC on the monthly view still has divergence, carrying the CEO-buying and re-positioning bull case alongside other voices. With 128 splits far outnumbering one-sided consensus, the 28-day period shows rapid rotation across themes.

Other Notes

70 common-bullish names versus only 18 common-bearish shows one-sided bearish views are relatively scarce. $NVDA has 424 mentions and $TSLA 468, extremely high attention without forming one-sided consensus. Total volume of 6510 posts indicates high information density, but direction still needs to be read from individual account reasons.

briefing.html:
Today's Briefing

Discussion volume rose to 62 posts over the past ~29 hours. The clearest consensus is on $INTC: two accounts re-read the same $55 level, one emphasizing it has become central to U.S. advanced chip manufacturing, the other highlighting the CEO’s fresh $10M buy and extreme RSI lows. $IREN also has two bullish accounts focusing on post-acquisition fundamentals and MSFT’s request to upgrade GB300, with residual caution on ATM size. The only common-bearish name is $ORCL, with the MSFT reduction of older $NVDA capacity still cited by @StockSavvyShay and @ripster47. $NVDA is most mentioned but sentiment has not formed a one-sided view. On the 7-day view $SPCX, $AAPL and $COHR show cleaner consensus while $ORCL’s $213 target contrasts with the capacity-reduction news; on the 28-day view $SOFI is the steadiest and the indices plus some AI infrastructure names remain highly split.
